title_or_table: American Community Survey 5-year estimates, Table B19013, Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars), with class and break crossings for the county map
geography: Every county and county equivalent of the 50 states and DC in the 2024 boundary files, in geoid order (Connecticut’s nine planning regions)
unit: 2024 dollars, with 90 percent margins of error
qualification: Five years of survey responses pooled, in 2024 dollars; margins are wide in small counties, so read classes with them. Connecticut’s counties are its planning regions, as in the 2024 boundary files. Classes: 1, under $50,000; 2, $50,000 to under $65,000; 3, $65,000 to under $80,000; 4, $80,000 or more; empty where the Bureau publishes no estimate (De Baca County, New Mexico).

name.description: county name and state, as the Bureau prints it

moe.description: 90 percent margin of error, as published

income_class.description: class under the breaks $50,000, $65,000 and $80,000, 1 to 4; empty with no estimate

breaks_crossed.description: breaks inside the 90 percent interval (value less margin to value plus margin), 0 to 3

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, Table B19013, median household income, 2020 to 2024, every county in the 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Survey estimates in 2024 dollars; margins are wide in small counties.
derivation: Each county's class by the data lead's breaks (round 3 ruling (c)) and the count of breaks strictly inside its 90 percent interval; rows in the geoid order of the boundary file census-cb-2024-counties.geojson, the national row left out (the map prints it beside itself) (cartographer_round3_derive.py)
notes: income classes [371, 1138, 1049, 585], none 1; intervals crossing a break 1707, two 182
